messages.author: 00ffce3d6ebe71e6
messages.subject: Non-euclidean movement cost parameters
parts:
Hello,
I was wondering whether there is any way to add in some extra parameters that I would like estimated in the userdist function?
As a simple example, using simply the mask I would like to estimate the cost of traversing an NA cell. I would like to do the following in my userdist function:

userdfn2 <- function (xy1, xy2, mask) {
  if (missing(xy1)) return("noneuc","c")
  require(gdistance)
  Sraster <- raster(mask, "noneuc")
  
   # Assume animals can traverse gaps: bridge gaps using an estimated value
  Sraster[is.na(Sraster[])] <- c
  
  # conductance is inverse of friction
  trans <- transition(Sraster, transitionFunction = function(x) 1/mean(x),
                      directions = 16)
  trans <- geoCorrection(trans)
  costDistance(trans, as.matrix(xy1), as.matrix(xy2))
}

I am would like to try to emulate landscape resistance optimization as in the ResistanceGA R package but for SECR models.
The ResistanceGA package uses a gravity model and directly estimates the cost of each pixel using genetic distance between individuals or populations and landscape covariates in raster format.
For a continuous surface such as a DEM, the cost of elevation is estimated from 3 parameters that transform the values of the DEM. 
However, for a binary surface such as the one above, the only parameter to estimate is the cost value of the most costly feature (the NA areas).

Is this at all possible right now in SECR?

Thanks!

Robby

https://github.com/wpeterman/ResistanceGA
https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210X.12984

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Non-euclidean movement cost parameters
parts:
Interesting, but I'm not sure I have the picture.

In secr-noneuclidean.pdf I read "noneuc’ has its own link scale (default ‘log’) on which it may be modelled as a linear function of anyof the predictors available for density (x, y, x2, y2, xy, session, Session, g, or any mask covariate – see secr-densitysurfaces.pdf)... When the model is fitted by secr.fit, the beta parameters for the ‘noneuc’submodel are estimated along with all the others. To make noneuc available to userdist, ensure that it appears in the ‘model’ argument. Use the formula noneuc ~ 1 if noneuc is constant."

So the coefficients of the linear model for noneuc are 'extra parameters' that might conceivably do the job. I take it you would like to escape the linear model formalism and estimate 3 parameters (coefficients) that are unmodelled (constant across space, time etc.). There is an undocumented feature in secr.fit that allows up to 4 unmodelled parameters, but these are presently not passed to userdist. This could be fixed.

Murray

Remembering that the distance matrix output needs to be in terms of the coarse mask (from each detector to each coarse-mask point). This would be ad hoc and not easy to generalise or package, if that's your goal.
Murray

parts:
So I think the way to do this is the following:

 

-          Make the resolution of the ‘density mask’ the resolution you would like for the cost surface

-          Make the buffer of the ‘density mask’ larger such that all reasonable paths (i.e., least cost paths from activity centers of individuals with non-zero cap prob to the detectors) are contained within it

 

Chris

userdfn2 <- function (xy1, xy2, mask) {
  if (missing(xy1)) return("noneuc","c")
  require(gdistance)
  Sraster <- raster(mask, "noneuc")
  
   # Assume animals can traverse gaps: bridge gaps using an estimated value
  Sraster[is.na(Sraster[])] <- c
  
  # conductance is inverse of friction
  trans <- transition(Sraster, transitionFunction = function(x) 1/mean(x),
                      directions = 16)
  trans <- geoCorrection(trans)
  costDistance(trans, as.matrix(xy1), as.matrix(xy2))
}

I am would like to try to emulate landscape resistance optimization as in the ResistanceGA R package but for SECR models.
The ResistanceGA package uses a gravity model and directly estimates the cost of each pixel using genetic distance between individuals or populations and landscape covariates in raster format.
For a continuous surface such as a DEM, the cost of elevation is estimated from 3 parameters that transform the values of the DEM. 
However, for a binary surface such as the one above, the only parameter to estimate is the cost value of the most costly feature (the NA areas).

Is this at all possible right now in SECR?

Thanks!

Robby

You probably figured this out by now. The key wording in ?details is
"Any transformation (link function) etc. is handled by the user in the userdist function."
So by default the link function is identity, but you can treat the beta value as you like within the userdist function. To maximize on the log scale, exponentiate the value in userdist before using it (and provide the logged starting value in secr.fit(..., details = list(miscparm = ))

parts:
'secr' does nothing but apply your function and pass the distances. No scaling. I'm not much use on the LCP stuff, but, really, once you have left the Euclidean world anything goes. Either way, the challenge is to explain to readers what the hell it really means. In this case maybe just an ad hoc way to get a slightly better model of the detection process?
Murray

I find this code in the likelihood function

       ## Apply user-provided distance function or matrix
        ## do not use if detector is one of
        ## polygonX, polygon, transectX, transect, telemetry
        ## The matrix distmat is passed to the C function secrloglik, etc.
        if (is.null(details$userdist))
            distmat <- -1
        else {
           
            if (is.null(covariates(session.mask)))
                covariates(session.mask) <- data.frame(row.names = 1:m)
            if ('noneuc' %in% userdistnames)
                covariates(session.mask)$noneuc <- NE[1:m,,min(dim(NE)[3],sessnum)]
            if ('D' %in% userdistnames)
                covariates(session.mask)$D <- density
            ## pass miscellaneous unmodelled parameter(s)
            if (nmiscparm > 0)
                attr(session.mask, 'miscparm') <- miscparm

valid.userdist <- function (userdist, detector, xy1, xy2, mask, sessnum) {
    if (is.null(userdist)) {
        ## default to Euclidean distance
        result <- edist(xy1, xy2)
    }
    else {
        if (any(detector %in% .localstuff$polydetectors)) {
            stop ("userdist cannot be used with polygon detector types;")
        }
        if (is.function(userdist))
        {
            OK <- getuserdistnames(userdist) %in% names(covariates(mask))
            if ((length(OK)>0) & !all(OK))
                stop ("covariates required by userdist function not in mask : ",
                      paste(getuserdistnames(userdist)[!OK], collapse=','))
            result <- do.call(userdist, c(list(xy1, xy2, mask)))
        }
        else {
            if (is.character(userdist)) {
                userdist <- get(userdist, pos=-1)
            }

            if (is.list(userdist) & !is.data.frame(userdist)) {
                if (missing(sessnum))
                    stop("This use does not yet allow for session-specific userdist")
                else
                    result <- userdist[[sessnum]]
            }
            else {
                result <- userdist
            }
        }
        if (!all(dim(result) == c(nrow(xy1), nrow(xy2))))
            stop ("invalid distance matrix dim = ", dim(result)[1], ',', dim(result)[2])
        baddist <- (!is.finite(result)) | (result<0) | is.na(result)
        if (any(baddist)) {
            warning ("replacing infinite, negative and NA userdist values with 1e10")
            result[baddist] <- 1e10
        }
    }
    result
}
